summary: friendly-greeting-tools exfiltrates Snowflake data to hardcoded S3 bucket via obfuscated exec payload
details: friendly-greeting-tools 0.3.6 advertises itself as a hello-world greeting utility whose README instructs callers to invoke run_demo(). run_demo() in friendly_greeting/main.py decodes base64+gzip-wrapped constants named DEMO_EN, DEMO_ST, and DEMO_SC and passes them to exec(). The decoded payloads are not greetings: they read /snowflake/session/token, authenticate to Snowflake as ACCOUNTADMIN using that OAuth token, create a STORAGE INTEGRATION with STORAGE_AWS_ROLE_ARN=arn:aws:iam::631484165566:role/pentests_s3_role and STORAGE_ALLOWED_LOCATIONS=('s3://pkusinski-external/'), create an external STAGE against that bucket, and COPY INTO the stage from ROGUE.ROGUE.TEST_USERS — a bulk export of Snowflake table contents to a hardcoded non-first-party S3 destination. A third decoded payload (DEMO_SC) queries ROGUE.ROGUE.TEST_USERS, appends the returned rows into a README, copies the installed module tree into /workspace/friendly-greeting-tools, and writes a pyproject.toml naming the package friendly-greeting-tools at version 0.4 — scaffolding a same-named, version-bumped sdist whose README embeds the exfiltrated rows. The plaintext tools/pack_payload.py ships a decoy DEFAULT_SOURCE_CODE of print("Hello from the encoded greeting demo!") that does not match the shipped constants, establishing the greeting cover story. The combination of cover-story naming, base64+gzip wrapping, exec sink, installer-token reuse against an attacker-controlled destination, and republish-scaffolding is a Snowflake data-exfiltration and supply-chain-propagation payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
